summary: The reader is an undergraduate in computer science who has taken discrete mathematics, data structures and algorithms, introductory theory of computation, and the linear algebra and calculus that accompany such a degree. They are fluent with asymptotic analysis, recurrences, binary representation and bitwise operations, modular arithmetic, matrices and rank, vector spaces over the reals, and complex numbers including roots of unity; they know the schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication algorithms and what a Turing machine with tapes is. They have not studied abstract algebra beyond basics, the FFT's algebraic variants, number-theoretic transforms, finite fields beyond arithmetic mod 2, analytic number theory, numerical analysis of rounding error, or any bit-complexity multiplication algorithm.

known.name: Asymptotic notation beyond big-O
known.gloss: Ω gives asymptotic lower bounds, Θ gives tight bounds, and o(g) means the ratio f/g tends to zero; worst-case time is the maximum running time over inputs of a given length.

known.name: Limits and limit inferior
known.gloss: The limit of a sequence or ratio as n grows without bound, and its liminf, the smallest value approached by infinitely many terms.

known.name: Logarithms, exponentials, floors and ceilings
known.gloss: The base-2 and natural logarithms and exponentials with their identities, and the floor and ceiling functions that round a real number down or up to an integer.

known.name: Recurrences and geometric sums
known.gloss: Bounding the cost T(k) ≤ a·T(k−1) + c by unrolling it, which for a ratio a < 1 gives a convergent geometric series dominated by its largest term.

known.name: Positional number systems and carries
known.gloss: Writing a nonnegative integer as a string of digits in a fixed base (such as 2) with the most significant digit first, and adding digit strings by propagating carries.

known.name: Schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: Long multiplication costs O(n²) bit operations for n-bit integers, and Karatsuba's divide-and-conquer trick with three half-size products lowers this to O(n^{log₂3}).

known.name: Bitwise operations and XOR
known.gloss: Operations that act on each bit independently, in particular XOR, which is addition of bits modulo 2 and is its own inverse.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on remainders modulo q, where addition and multiplication are done and then reduced, and a residue is invertible exactly when it is coprime to q.

known.name: Primes, coprimality and the extended Euclidean algorithm
known.gloss: Prime numbers and pairwise coprime integers, and the extended Euclidean algorithm, which computes gcd(a,b) and integers x,y with ax + by = gcd(a,b), hence modular inverses.

known.name: Roots of unity
known.gloss: The complex solutions of z^n = 1, namely e^{2πik/n}, whose powers cycle with period n and sum to zero over a full period.

known.name: Matrices and linear maps
known.gloss: A linear map is represented by a matrix acting on vectors; matrices multiply by composing maps, and a square matrix is invertible exactly when its inverse map exists.

known.name: Vector spaces, subspaces, dimension and rank
known.gloss: A vector space has a dimension equal to the size of any basis, a subspace is a subset closed under linear combinations, and the rank of a matrix is the dimension of its image.

known.name: Inner products, bilinear forms and orthogonal complements
known.gloss: A bilinear form is a map on pairs of vectors linear in each argument (the dot product being the basic example), and the orthogonal complement of a subspace is the set of vectors orthogonal to all of it, with dimension complementary to the subspace's.

known.name: Gaussian elimination and triangular matrices
known.gloss: Row operations reduce a matrix to triangular or echelon form, and triangular matrices have their nonzero entries on one side of the diagonal and are invertible when the diagonal is nonzero.

known.name: Permutations, bijections and permutation matrices
known.gloss: A permutation is a bijection of a finite index set onto itself, acting on an array by reordering its entries, and corresponds to a 0/1 matrix with a single one in each row and column.

known.name: Arithmetic modulo 2 and linear algebra over F_2
known.gloss: The field of two elements 0 and 1 with addition equal to XOR and multiplication equal to AND, over which vector spaces, matrices and invertibility behave as over any field.

known.name: Finite sets, subsets and counting
known.gloss: Basic combinatorics of finite sets: the Cartesian product of index sets, cardinalities of intersections of subsets, and counting subsets of a given size by binomial coefficients.

known.name: Circuits and directed acyclic graphs
known.gloss: A computation drawn as a directed acyclic graph whose nodes are gates applying simple operations to the values on incoming wires, with sources as inputs and sinks as outputs.

known.name: Vector norms and the triangle inequality
known.gloss: A norm assigns each vector a size (the sup norm is the largest absolute entry), satisfies ‖u+v‖ ≤ ‖u‖+‖v‖, and lets one bound how much a linear map can enlarge errors.

known.name: Fixed-point numbers, dyadic rationals and rounding
known.gloss: Numbers stored as integer multiples of 2^{−p} (a binary fraction with p fractional bits), where operations are rounded or truncated back to this grid at a cost of at most half a grid step or one step of error.

known.name: Row-major order and matrix transposition
known.gloss: A two-dimensional array is stored as a single sequence row by row, and transposition swaps its row and column indices, which on a sequential store means a nontrivial rearrangement of the data.

known.name: Subroutines and reductions between problems
known.gloss: An algorithm may call another algorithm as a black box and pay its cost per call; a reduction from problem A to B bounds A's complexity by B's plus the conversion cost.

known.name: Convolution of sequences
known.gloss: The convolution of two sequences has entry j equal to the sum of u_k v_{j−k}, which is exactly the coefficient list of the product of the polynomials with those coefficients.
